lines.say: How much water do you need when you lift?
Losing just two percent of your body weight in sweat can lower your endurance, and a bit of your strength.
A simple test: check your pee. Pale yellow is good. Dark yellow means drink more.
Guidelines suggest drinking some water a few hours before training, and sipping during it.
Weigh yourself before and after a long, sweaty session. For each kilo lost, drink about one and a half litres over the next hours.
Too much water, too fast, can also be dangerous. Don't force litres you don't need.
Thirst and your pee colour are your best guides.
